cohort: 100 women with a fetus in the occipital posterior position, 60 of whom underwent low forceps-assisted delivery and 40 of whom underwent cesarean section; 60 primiparous women with a fetus in the occipital anterior position who underwent low forceps-assisted delivery served as a control group
finding: For women with a prolonged second stage of labor and a fetus in the occipital posterior position, low forceps-assisted delivery was associated with shorter delivery times, reduced bleeding, fewer infections, shorter hospital stays, and lower costs compared to cesarean section, without increasing adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study specifically investigates the impact of delivery methods in the context of a prolonged second stage of labor.
